correctness.rationale: For λ>2, the finite left-path Dirichlet recurrence gives p_{k-1}/p_k and the square-summable right tail gives t. Their exact matching equation F_k=0 is strictly increasing in λ, and F_k(2+) determines the sharp phase threshold. The finite-path resolvent ratio increases strictly with k, proving monotonicity. The exact t-formula shows uniform convergence of F_k and derivatives near the limiting root; the mean-value theorem yields the nonzero coefficient a²(s−1)²/(4s²) after scaling s^{k+1/2}. The essential spectrum is [-2,2] by finite-rank perturbation. Critical resonance is not an ℓ² eigenvector. Packaged rational and numerical checks corroborate, rather than prove, the unbounded-index assertion.

originality.rationale: The 2015 full-text finitely perturbed weighted-shift paper supplies the general Jacobi characteristic framework but not a position-asymptotic theorem. The new claim quantifies the exact isolated-eigenvalue threshold at each boundary distance and the nonzero exponentially small leading coefficient as distance increases, with orientation dependence. The 2014 adjacent-weight finite-path theorems and 2013 one-defect operator examples are not stronger forms. Published mathematical-search records gave no matching claim. A closely relevant 2015 determinantal-polynomial paper was available only at abstract level, so priority is not externally certified and residual risk is stated.
residual_risks: The complete text of Chien–Nakazato–Undrakh–Vandanjav (2015 online) was inaccessible; it might already derive the translated two-bond coefficient or a dominating formula.
A more general off-diagonal Jacobi boundary perturbation theorem could imply the exact exponentially small leading coefficient without using weighted-shift terminology.

The broad 2015 ELA characteristic polynomial is a starting point and logically encodes fixed-k values; this makes the additional uniform asymptotic the substantive claimed advance, not the polynomial itself.

value.rationale: The operator is a natural half-line two-bond perturbation of the unilateral shift. The exact k-dependent inequality classifies boundary-induced bound-state birth, including a finite plateau and strict onset. The explicit first exponential correction quantifies spectral localization and distinguishes order of adjacent impurity strengths, despite an order-independent infinite-volume limit. This is a structural asymptotic theorem rather than a small numerical improvement or a routine evaluation for one dimension.
